_readme: The demo dataset. Every person, company, address and message in this file is invented.
Dates are stored as offsets, never as absolute stamps, so the demo is a live working week
on whatever day someone opens it. `day` is a whole-day offset from the visitor's today
(0 = today, -1 = yesterday, 2 = the day after tomorrow) and `time` is wall-clock 24h.
demo/lib/api.js materialises them into ISO strings carrying the visitor's own UTC offset,
which is what the calendar reads its chip positions off.
demo/lib/demo-data.js is generated from this file by demo/build-data.mjs and is what the
page actually imports — a static ESM import means the demo makes no network request at all,
not even for its own data.

drafts.subject: Re: Diligence — retention and the hosting line
drafts.body:
Yuki,

Apologies for the gap. Both answers below.

Retention: 91% of accounts that reach month three are still with us at month twelve, and the cohort split is in the attached sheet — the dip you spotted in the February cohort was one reseller consolidating eleven accounts into two, not eleven cancellations.

Hosting: the line grows with storage, not with headcount, which is why it looks disconnected from revenue. At current growth it is £2,100 a month by the end of next year, and it moves to a reserved-instance rate at the point that is worth doing.

Happy to walk either of them through on a call this week.

Ivo

drafts.subject: Introduction — Brightsea
drafts.body:
Tobias,

I owe you this and I have sat on it for far too long.

The right person at Brightsea is Yuki Tamsin, who runs their early-stage work and has spent the last year looking specifically at instrumentation. I have copied her here.

Yuki — Tobias runs Cassowary Labs. They build the measurement layer that the last two hardware companies you asked me about were missing. Worth an hour.

I will get out of the way.

Ivo

drafts.subject: Re: Revised haulage quote
drafts.body:
Aurelio,

Chasing the revised haulage figure — you had said Tuesday and I know last week ran away from everyone.

I can hold the tender until Thursday morning without it, but not past that; the rest of the price is built and yours is the only number still open.

If the revision is going to take longer, send me the old figure with a plus-or-minus and I will work with that.

Ivo

drafts.subject: Fenwick — conflict check
drafts.body:
Priya,

On the conflict question: we have no live engagement with Fenwick Dairy Co-op and no work for anyone on the other side of the co-op's supply agreement. The only prior contact is a feasibility sketch in 2023 that was never invoiced and never left the studio.

As far as I can see there is nothing to declare, but you have the better view of what counts.

The kickoff is in two days, so if you need anything else from me to open the matter, say so today.

Ivo

Also — and I keep forgetting to say this properly — the grant window closes with the quarter, so anything we want covered by it has to be committed before then.

scripts.answer:
Desmond Okafor at Pentland Civil needs the bond rider signed by you before the surety desk closes at five today. He has asked twice — once three days ago when he signed Pentland's side, and again this morning to say the filing goes in at four.

He has also told you the escape hatch: sign the page, photograph it, send the photograph. The surety has accepted that before.

There is a walkthrough with him on your calendar at 11 this morning, which is the last moment this is a conversation rather than a chase.

Yuki Tamsin at Brightsea asked you two questions six days ago and has had no answer.

One: retention by cohort rather than in aggregate — she specifically wants to see the February shape, which the aggregate hides. Two: why the hosting line in your model grows faster than revenue.

You also told her, in writing, that the retention numbers would be with her by Wednesday. That is tomorrow. There is a draft reply waiting in Owed that answers both — the February dip was a reseller consolidating eleven accounts into two.

Her partner meeting is a week today, which is the real deadline underneath the stated one.

The Fenwick kickoff is in two days, from 10 until 12, at the co-op in Ballynure. Three things are attached to it.

Priya Ardmore cannot open the matter until you confirm in writing that there is no conflict — she asked two days ago and a sentence is enough. There is a draft in Owed that says it.

The Meridian freight walkthrough is booked for 10:30 the same morning, straight over the top of it. Aurelio has already offered the following day and said the yard is quieter then.

And Roisin mentioned once, in a thread about scaffolding, that the grant window closes with the quarter. Nobody has done anything with that.

Three people owe you something and three people are owed something by you.

Owed to you: the borough has sat on the hoarding permit for sixteen days with no reference number, which is blocking the site fence. Meridian owe the revised haulage quote — Aurelio said Tuesday, eight days ago. Ardmore & Vance have had the redline for five days against a two-day turnaround.

Owed by you: retention numbers to Yuki by tomorrow, an introduction you promised Tobias twelve days ago, and one sentence of photography credit to Imogen.

Separately, Halloran Rowe are 41 days late on invoice 2214 — £8,650, and the fourth late invoice in a row.

Two live money items and one administrative one.

Out: the Quarrymen invoice for phase two stonework, £14,280, measured and agreed on site. Nils pays his crew on Friday and has said an approval before then keeps him out of his own overdraft.

In: Halloran Rowe, invoice 2214, £8,650, 41 days overdue. Marguerite last replied twelve days ago to say it was with their finance people. It is the fourth late one in a row and the previous two each needed a phone call.

And Dermot Finch at Sable & Finch has asked four times for the March to June receipts. He has stopped being annoyed and started being polite about it, which is worse.

First: the Pentland bond rider. It is the only thing today with a hard external cut-off — the surety desk shuts at five and after that it is next week.

Then the Brightsea answers, because six days of silence on an open term sheet is doing damage that a late reply cannot undo but an absent one compounds.

Then RFI 214 — the steel fabricator has downed tools on that assembly and is waiting on one connection detail.

Your calendar has a problem at half past one: lunch with Dermot Finch and the RFI call are booked over each other. Given that RFI 214 is on the board and Dermot has asked for receipts four times, neither is obviously the one to drop.

Two collisions this week.

Today at 13:30 the RFI 214 call with the steel fabricator runs straight into lunch with Dermot Finch, which starts at one. Half an hour of overlap and both of them think they have you.

In two days the Meridian freight walkthrough at 10:30 sits inside the Fenwick kickoff, which runs 10 until 12 and is an hour's drive from the Meridian yard. That one is not a scheduling problem, it is a choice — and Aurelio has already offered the following day.

Everything else in the week is clean.
